podcast.body: "Fulfillingness' First Finale" is among the three highly important albums Stevie Wonder released in the 1970s, all composed and recorded using the TONTO synthesizer with Malcolm Cecil and Robert Margouleff. These records significantly changed the direction of Wonder's career and influenced Black Pop music. "It was talking book, intervisions, and fulfilling this first finale."

podcast.body: Released in the summer of 1974 as a follow-up to "Innervisions," this album's momentum was boosted by the previous Grammy win, sending it to number one on the charts. It subsequently won the top prize at the 1975 Grammy Awards, marking Wonder's second consecutive Album of the Year win. "And then that summer, Wonder dropped his follow-up LP, Fulfilliness First Finale. And this time, the momentum from the Grammy win sent the album to number one. And then, Fulfilliness won the top prize at the 75 Grammy Awards."

podcast.body: Stevie Wonder won a Grammy for this album in 1974. This accomplishment was noted as part of the "awesomeness" of music in 1974, alongside Olivia Newton-John's Grammy win for "I Honestly Love You." "Stevie Wonder won for the album Fulfillingness's first finale."

Stevie Wonder, known as a perfectionist, took two years to release a follow-up to this album, causing restlessness among fans and industry members who wondered if he might retire. "It had been two years since the noted perfectionist Stevie Wonder had released fulfilling this is first finale in the music industry."

podcast.body: The second in a sequence of three career-defining albums for Stevie Wonder, this record preceded *Songs in the Key of Life*. "This is the third in his string of three career defining albums, beginning with Intervisions in 1972, Fulfillingness's First Finale in 1974, and now the Songs of Key of Life."
